tables.title: Current National Problems
values: Farmland is becoming worn-out and depleted — old Roman drainage has failed and bogs are returning
Verminous monsters are swarming from the fens, moors, or barrows
A rebel front is stirring up trouble against the High King or regional lord
A foreign power is backing internal strife — Saxon lords, Irish pirates, or a rival British king
The leadership is inept and distracted by private pleasures or petty quarrels
A religious reformer is breaking old compacts between church and secular power
An evil is provoking outraged rioting — a dark cult, a monstrous tribute, an unjust judgment
Dark cults are attracting the ambitious and the desperate
A Saxon or Pictish horde is threatening the borders
An ancient ruin has disgorged some peril — barrow-wights, a bound evil, a faerie court angered
Malcontents have obtained a potent relic and are using it against the kingdom
Luxuriance has left the king's coffers bare — a great feast, a failed campaign, a royal ransom
Local lords are pushing for independence or refusing to send levies
An important mine or resource site has run out or been seized by enemies
A sinister favourite has infatuated the lord — a foreign sorceress, a corrupt churchman, a flatterer
A recurring cattle plague or crop blight is causing hunger
Fearsome monsters are migrating into settled lands from the wilderness
A rival king is preparing for war or raiding
A grand national plan is exhausting the people — road-building, a fortress, a campaign
A savage grudge has erupted into open violence between two great lords

tables.title: Good Things Happening Right Now
values: A splendid mine, holy spring, or resource has been found
A pious holy man or woman is strengthening the Church and drawing pilgrims
A noble heir shows signs of heroic greatness — strength, wisdom, unusual piety
A major rival has recently suffered a calamity and cannot threaten the kingdom
New farmland has been drained or cleared and families are settling it
A new trade route has been forged — to a distant port, across the moors, through the forest
A horrible monster was slain or driven off, and the villages are safe
Good harvests have enriched the people and the granaries are full
A wicked minister or corrupt official has been deposed and punished
A new school, monastery, or scriptorium has recently opened
A bandit or rebel uprising has been crushed
Two rival lords have begun to make peace — a marriage has been proposed
An old enemy has agreed to a truce or peace pact
The military won a recent smashing victory
A useful relic or faerie-gift has been activated or recovered
A powerful relic is helping the ruler govern and judge
An old source of unrest — a blood feud, a territorial dispute — has been calmed
A dark cult has been revealed and purged from a major community
New diplomatic ties have been made with a former enemy
A new lord has risen, loved by his people for his justice and generosity

tables.title: Disputes With a Neighbouring Power
values: Raiders are taking refuge in their lands after striking ours
Ownership of a resource site — a mine, a ford, a fishing ground — is disputed
A usurper or criminal is being sheltered by them
A troublemaking religious sect is based in their territory
Their rulers have a political claim on our throne or on land we hold
A diplomatic marriage has gone sour — insults were given, a bride mistreated
A past war's savagery has left deep scars that have not healed
Their culture or religion is supplanting local beliefs among our people
Their immigrants are gaining great influence in border communities
They broke off an alliance or an important oath
They lured away a respected scholar, holy man, or craftsman
Border tariffs and tolls are blocking trade and enriching bandits
They drove a terrible monster or cursed tribe into our land
A faerie mound or Roman ruin they tampered with has sent evil into our territory
They woke up a great peril from the past
They are cooperating with our enemies — harbouring Saxon scouts, supplying raiders
They are suspected of backing assassinations or palace intrigues here
A spy ring operating from their court has been found or is suspected
They refused to give aid for some current crisis
They have been hostile to an allied group or vassal of ours

tables.title: Positive Ties With a Neighbouring Power
values: The ruling classes are related — a marriage, a shared ancestor
An important faith crosses the border and unites the peoples
They fought beside us in some famous battle within living memory
Their culture is widely admired here — their bards, their smithwork, their horses
They helped us overcome an otherworldly or monstrous peril
They held back an enemy from our border when we could not
They are co-ethnics of the same British origin
They provide critical trade goods we cannot make ourselves
Scholars and holy men came from there and founded our greatest institutions
They gave critical aid during a plague, famine, or disaster
A hero of this land came originally from there
A past hero-king once ruled both lands
They produce some vital commodity — grain, tin, horses, salt
We share a dangerous enemy
A holy site or relic that helps us lies within their borders
A long-standing alliance or trade pact exists
They recently conceded some disputed land or right
They greatly admire elements of our culture
They are considered unusually desirable marriage partners
They took in our refugees at some past time of great need

entries.value: Barbarian invasion — Saxons, Picts, Irish, or some older terror
Colonial incursion from a greater power — Rome, or a former Roman province
Decadent society — internal collapse of values and will
Divine wrath upon them — plague, famine, drought sent as punishment
Domineering neighbour — tribute demanded, hostages taken, autonomy stripped
Economic collapse — trade routes cut, coinage debased, silver mines exhausted
Failed external war — a campaign that ruined the fighting men and emptied the granaries
Ideological divide — a religious schism, a dispute over custom, a heresy
Incompetent governance — a succession of bad rulers, a regency disaster
Internal refugees from disaster — famine, flood, or burning drove people from their homes
Loss of cultural confidence — a humiliation so great the people doubted their own worth
Magical calamity — a curse laid on the land, a faerie war, a sorcerer's blunder
Malevolent religion — a dark cult seized power, demanded tribute, corrupted the church
Miserable poverty — generations of hunger and bare survival
Natural disasters — floods, drought, bitter winters, plague of animals
Noble infighting — the lords tore themselves apart in blood feud and petty war
Religious or ideological excess — a purge, a crusade, a witch-hunt
Resource exhaustion — the forest, mine, or fishing grounds gave out
Scheming sorcerers — wizards manipulated or preyed upon the people
Some titanic monster — a dragon, a giant, a faerie lord turned enemy
Tyrannical rule — a warlord or corrupt king squeezed the people dry
Unsuccessful expansion — a war of conquest that went badly and cost everything
Usurpers seizing control — a coup, a betrayal, a false claimant
Vicious civil warfare — the people turned on each other
War with a stronger power — a devastating defeat from which recovery was slow

tables.title: How Did They Overcome the Crisis?
values: A brilliant and inspirational leader arose
Organisation and unity overcame the trouble
Grim determination and simply enduring the evil
Faith strengthened them against the woe
Skilful use of magic or knowledge resolved the problem
Martial prowess and military cunning
Diplomatic ties and outside help
Industrious labour and tireless exertion
Economic brilliance and trading acumen
Ruthless but effective sacrifices were made

tables.title: Why Did They Fail At the Final Crisis?
values: Their people were too deeply divided
Their leadership was hopelessly inept
The gods cursed them to ruin
Decadence and self-absorption doomed them
They were vastly overconfident in their plans
Their neighbours conspired to help ruin them
It was actually two crises, and it was too much
They were culturally exhausted and apathetic
Some tried to take advantage of the crisis themselves
Their strengths were useless against this particular problem
The crisis was far too vast and overwhelming
Some of their leaders were allied with the crisis

entries.value: **Battleground:** The group's territory ended up as a battleground between two stronger rivals, and they suffered bitterly for it.
**Betrayal:** Either they betrayed some trusting neighbour to a foe, or were betrayed in turn by such a false friend.
**Brutal Oppression:** Some portion of the group was reduced to wretched subservience by the rest.
**Class Struggle:** Different classes were in conflict, either subtle or overt, all seeking their own gain.
**Consequences:** Pick an event of a prior age; it had long-term consequences — good for a bad event, or bad for a good event.
**Decadence:** Old strengths and glories crumbled away into decadent remnants, the group becoming indolent and indulgent.
**Depravity:** Vile debauches and base hungers became commonplace among the group.
**Desolation:** Some portion of the group's territory was rendered uninhabitable — blighted, flooded, cursed.
**Diplomatic Coup:** The group achieved an extremely successful alliance or marriage-tie with a neighbouring power.
**Economic Boom:** Circumstances produced a burst of tremendous prosperity.
**Enemies Within:** A hostile sub-group inside the group worked to do it evil, perhaps on behalf of a neighbour.
**Evil Sorcerer:** A malevolent sorcerer, arcane cult, or powerful faerie entity caused a great deal of trouble.
**Exodus:** A significant chunk of the group packed up and left for some supposedly-superior land.
**Exquisite Art:** The group produced art that is revered to this day.
**External War:** The group faced a war with some external enemy or rival nation, with grave consequences.
**Freakish Magic:** A particular type of magic was developed here that is unknown elsewhere, and its practitioners keep its secrets.
**Golden Age:** Everything went remarkably well for the group for an extended period, allowing prosperity and success.
**Good Sorcerer:** Some magic-using entity of great power protected the group, taught them, or otherwise assisted them.
**Great Awakening:** A tremendous wave of reform, purification, and re-commitment to venerable values swept through the group.
**Great Builders:** The group constructed a great many vast palaces, monuments, estates, or other structures of wide fame.
**Great Infrastructure:** Some tremendous work of infrastructure was accomplished: roads, walls, aqueducts, drainage, mines.
**Hero King:** Some ruler achieved legendary glory in war, diplomacy, or governance. Their name is honoured even today.
**Immigrants:** A large group of foreigners entered the land more-or-less peacefully and may or may not have been welcomed.
**Inefficient Rule:** The group's governance was impractical, inefficient, or corrupt.
**Internal War:** A straight-up civil war was sparked in the group, one that involved all or many of its members.
**Loss of Confidence:** Some encounter with a new group or some shocking event made the group lose faith in its own customs.
**Magical Disaster:** Some large-scale magical disaster scarred the group — a sorcerer's folly, a faerie war, a curse.
**Magical Tech:** The group developed a useful widespread relic or magical infrastructure that may have survived into the present.
**Natural Calamity:** Earthquakes, multi-year droughts, storms, or some other ruin smote the group.
**New Horizons:** The group discovered new territory — a hidden valley, an island, a passage through the mountains.
**New Rulers:** The group's former ruling dynasty was replaced, either peacefully, through intrigue, or through outright conquest.
**Noble Function:** The ruling class was all expected to fill some specific role: priest, sorcerer, judge, warrior.
**Noble Strife:** The group's nobility found itself embroiled in assassinations, petty wars, and mutual struggle.
**Plague:** A sickness of vast scope culled many of the group, and may yet linger in some form.
**Poverty:** Circumstances conspired to reduce the group to great poverty and harsh simplicity for a time.
**Power Brokers:** The group was a critical regional power broker, their aid or influence critical in determining who would be king.
**Praetorian Coups:** Warriors or household guards in service to the ruler ended up becoming the ruler's electors or deposers.
**Priest King:** One or more religions became deeply intertwined with the legitimacy of the ruling class.
**Rare Resource:** Some unique and precious material was found or produced by the group.
**Religious Fall:** A formerly-powerful faith collapsed or was driven out, leaving a vacuum.
**Religious Rise:** A new or previously-minor faith grew dramatically in power and influence.
**Resource Collapse:** A critical resource the group depended on failed them — mine exhausted, forests cut, herds diseased.
**Ruinous Alliance:** The group allied with what seemed like a powerful benefactor that proved to be a catastrophic mistake.
**Schism:** The group split internally along ideological, ethnic, or religious lines.
**Slaughter:** The group suffered a catastrophic loss of population to warfare, plague, or famine.
**Trade Dominance:** The group controlled the trade of the entire region for a time.
**Usurpation:** The proper ruling line was deposed by a claimant, creating legitimacy disputes that persist today.
**Venerable Relic:** A sacred object was created, found, or lost during this period — its current whereabouts are unknown.
**Xenophobia:** The group turned inward, driving out or oppressing a minority that had previously been tolerated.
**Roll Twice:** Both events happened in the same generation, intertwined.

tables.title: Current Struggle Within a Government
values: The lord is trying to crush a too-powerful vassal who has grown dangerous
Ministers or bishops are trying to usurp power from the lord
A grand scheme — a war, a monument, a marriage — has gone terribly wrong
External diplomacy has bungled something and caused a crisis
A usurper secretly controls a major institution
Foreign rivals are backing malcontents inside the court
A different class — merchants, commoners, lesser clergy — demands a share of rule
The existing ruling class wants more power and is willing to cause disruption to get it
A disfavoured class is being oppressed, and the injustice is generating resistance
Popular discontent is eroding the lord's legitimacy
The prior lord's incompetence or mistakes still constrain the current one
The heir is unacceptable to many powerful people for some reason

tables.title: Recent Governmental Events
values: A major official was executed or exiled for treason
A critically-necessary heir was born, or confirmed, or announced
A chief minister fell rapidly from grace
A high noble made openly rebellious noises
A major faith was offended by the lord's actions
An allied lord was angered by some act of the court
An enemy's spy ring was revealed operating inside the court
A vast governmental project was announced — a campaign, a fortress, a pilgrimage
Corrupt officials plundered a great plan and it has failed
A new council, charter, or institution was formed
A heavy levy was imposed on the people to deal with some crisis
A general or warlord was dismissed for incompetence or insubordination
A folk hero rose to dangerous popularity among the common people
A major infrastructure project was begun — a road, a bridge, a church
A fief or territory was put in new hands, angering the previous holder's kin
Certain merchants or nobles were ruined by fines or seizure of their goods
A terrorist attack by rebels, Saxon agents, or faerie agents
A major faction of court officials collapsed or was purged
A significant privilege or exemption was revoked
Province or hundred borders were redrawn, causing local fury

tables.title: Officials Causing Problems
values: Rapaciously grasping tax-farmers or rent collectors
Ill-disciplined and thieving soldiers or retainers
Bribe-hungry and meddling magistrates
Ever-watchful informers among neighbours
Tithe-hungry collectors from the Church or a religious house
Corrupt and untrustworthy market officials
Carelessly superior nobles and their retinues
Thuggish constables or town guards
Pitiless inquisitors hunting out dark paganism or heresy
Law enforcers acting as if they are above the law
State or church scholars teaching vile or politically-dangerous principles
Corrupt village headmen acting as petty tyrants

tables.title: Form of the Betrayal
values: They were never loyal — they were an enemy agent from the beginning
They sold the players out to save their own life or property
They were threatened or blackmailed into it
They made a worse deal than the one they had with the players
They genuinely changed their mind and now believe the players are in the wrong
They panicked and gave up information under pressure without meaning to betray
They were deceived into betraying without realising that was what they were doing
Their loyalty was to something higher — their lord, their god, their family — not to the players
They were seduced or enchanted into disloyalty
A past grudge they never disclosed motivated everything all along

tables.title: When It Is Discovered
values: Immediately — the players watch it happen
Shortly after — they find evidence within the same session
After the fact — they have to piece it together from consequences
By a third party who tells them
Long after — the damage is already done
Never conclusively — they suspect but cannot prove

tables.title: What the Betrayer Wanted
values: Their own safety — they feared the consequences of loyalty more than disloyalty
Wealth — they were simply paid enough to turn
Protection of a loved one — someone they care about was threatened
Advancement — loyalty to the players was a dead end
Revenge — some old wrong, real or imagined, that the players did not know about
Ideological — they genuinely believe the players' enemies are right
Desperation — they had no good options left and this seemed least bad
Cowardice — they simply could not hold firm under pressure

tables.title: What Goes Wrong: Sudden Complications
values: The person they needed to speak to is dead, missing, or unreachable
A third party they did not account for arrives with their own agenda
The information they acted on was deliberately false
An ally changes sides — not necessarily against the players, but toward their own interests
The time available is suddenly much shorter than assumed
A prior action of the players has come back to haunt them here
The target has moved — the person, object, or situation is elsewhere
Natural disaster or weather makes the situation much worse
A superior authority intervenes and takes jurisdiction away from the players
Someone who should be an enemy turns out to be a potential ally
A secret comes to light that changes everyone's understanding of the situation
The obvious solution is unavailable because of some constraint no one mentioned
An innocent person is now in danger as a consequence of the players' actions
The Enemy knows what the players are planning
The Friend who promised to help cannot — they are compromised, frightened, or gone
The Thing turns out to be not what the players thought it was
Someone important to the players is taken as a hostage or leverage
The players are blamed for something they did not do
An old wound is reopened — a blood feud, a broken oath, a past insult
Everything goes well, but the consequences of success are unexpectedly complicated

tables.title: Themes for a Region or Kingdom
values: **Barbarism** — brutal savagery is always near the surface
**Decadence** — sins and fadings; voluptuous cruelty and indolence
**Despair** — hopelessness and apathetic submission; the golden age is clearly lost
**Exhaustion** — strength spent and lost; everything is tired here
**Ignorance** — superstition and erroneous beliefs are critical to the culture's survival
**Oppression** — rule is a crushing weight; whole groups suffer under its heel
**Poverty** — even the rich are poor; the struggle for basics drives all conflict
**Precarity** — all goods are made fleeting; venerable institutions are tottering
**Stratification** — classes do not touch; the adventurer is a wild card here
**Violence** — life is something cheap; death in bed is a thing unlooked-for
**Enlightenment** — knowledge is loved; academies and scripture have real influence
**Expansion** — things swell greater; the people are vigorous and confident
**Hope** — the future should be better; a new lord, a new relic, a new alliance
**Justice** — a reckoning is coming; institutions of honest judgment are powerful here
**Legitimacy** — rulers are by right; it is almost unthinkable to overthrow them
**Pageantry** — splendour and magnificence; great feasts, grand processions, magnificent churches
**Prosperity** — wealth is easily had; the average family eats well
**Renewal** — things are growing brighter; old houses reviving, old wrongs being righted
**Triumph** — a victory is fresh in the memory; the people are confident and the enemies are weak
**Unity** — purposes are shared; the people paper over internal conflicts to face common threats

tables.title: Saxon and Pictish Threat Complications
values: A Saxon war-band has made a deal with a local British lord against his neighbours
The Saxons raided a holy site and took a relic — they do not know what it is
Saxon settlers are farming land that was abandoned, and locals want it back
A Pictish raid from the north has been confused with a Saxon one, and the wrong people are being blamed
A British lord has offered Saxon foederati land in exchange for military service; the surrounding lords are furious
Saxon children taken as hostages during a treaty have grown up and now serve at a British court
A Saxon noble has converted to Christianity and is now protected by the Church, to everyone's frustration
The Saxon shore fortifications are falling into ruin — someone is supposed to maintain them but is not

tables.title: Church and Pagan Complications
values: A holy well the Church has claimed was previously sacred to a pagan goddess and her followers are furious
A bishop and a local sorcerer have a long-running feud that everyone is being forced to take sides in
A relic is discovered that the Church and the pagan community both claim as their own
A heresy is spreading — one that holds that the old pagan powers were merely lesser gods, not demons
A group of monks is copying old Roman or pre-Roman texts; the local bishop wants them burned
A pagan harvest rite that everyone in the village takes part in has been declared sinful
A faerie bargain struck by the ancestors still binds the Church's land — the Church cannot break it without terrible consequences
A saint's tomb is producing miracles, but the miracles are the wrong kind — old, earthy, pagan in character

tables.title: Faerie and Otherworldly Complications
values: A faerie lord claims a debt is owed by a local noble's lineage — and the debt is centuries old
A child has been swapped for a changeling; the parents have noticed but are afraid to say so
A river has changed course and flooded fields that were not flooded before; the river-spirit is angry about something
A knight has returned from the Perilous Forest after what seemed like a year but was actually seven years — and no one knows what to do with him
A faerie bargain that protected the village from harm has expired; no one knows what it required in return
A stream that flows through a village has water that heals wounds but slowly drives those who drink it mad
A barrow has opened; the dead are not hostile, but they are asking questions that no one wants to answer
A forest has been slowly advancing over the past generation; the trees are moving
